Situation Report on the 17th Outbreak of EBOLA Virus Disease /RDC

SitRep N°25/MVB_08/06/2026

Affected Provinces (3) ITURI, NORD-KIVU & SUD-KIVU

Affected Health Zones (25)

Ituri (17/36): Aru, Aungba, Bambu, Bunia, Damas, Gety, Kilo, Komanda, Lita, Logo, Mambasa, Mangala, Mongbwalu, Nizi, Nyankunde, Rimba, Rwampara

Nord-Kivu (7/34): Beni, Butembo, Goma, Kalunguta, Katwa, Kyondo, Oicha

Sud-Kivu (1/34): Miti-Murhesa

Reporting date 08 June 2026

Publication date 09 June 2026

[PHOTO]

# 1. HIGHLIGHTS

During the day of 08 June 2026, 48 new confirmed cases including 14 deaths, were reported in the provinces of Ituri and Nord-Kivu.

These are distributed across the health zones of Mongbwalu (16), Bunia (11), Rwampara (11), Nyankunde (6) and Aungba (1) in Ituri, Butembo (2) and Katwa (1) in Nord-Kivu.

Three (3) confirmed patients of Ebola virus disease from the ZS (health zone) of Rwampara (Ituri province) were declared cured.

# 2. EPIDEMIOLOGICAL AND OPERATIONAL CONTEXT

Ituri province, located in the north-east of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, shares a long and porous border with Uganda and South Sudan.

For more than two decades, it has been facing a chronic humanitarian crisis linked to armed conflicts and recurrent population displacements.

Its population is estimated at more than 8 million inhabitants, including more than one million internally displaced persons.

The Mongbwalu health zone, considered as the starting point of the epidemic, is located in the territory of Djugu 70 km from Bunia.

This zone is characterised by the presence of armed groups, frequent population movements towards Uganda, and numerous artisanal mining sites attracting migrant workers.

In September 2018, Ituri province had already been affected by the 10th MVE (Ebola virus disease) outbreak which was then raging in Nord-Kivu.

The current outbreak, due to Bundibugyo ebolavirus, was officially declared on 15 May 2026 by the Minister of Public Health.

The three affected provinces have a total population estimated at nearly 15 million inhabitants, with massive internal displacements and cross-border flows towards neighbouring countries.

[FIGURE: Figure 1. Chronology of events of the Ebola-Bundibugyo virus disease outbreak.]

No new health zone was affected at the end of the day of 08 June 2026.

Ituri province accounts for 94,1% of confirmed cases reported in the 3 affected provinces.

Nord-Kivu province remains the most affected in terms of case fatality (68,7%) while Ituri province maintains a low case fatality (16,3%).

The situation remains static in Sud-Kivu province, which had recorded its last confirmed case on 26 May 2026.

## 3.3 Temporal analysis:

An increasing number of confirmed cases is observed from one week to the next, reflecting continuous transmission of the disease in the community.

A sudden geographical expansion of the epidemic is to be feared if public health actions are not implemented rapidly.

# 4. RESPONSE ACTIONS BY PILLAR

## 4.1 Coordination

National / Ituri:

Organisation of a community dialogue by the DG of the INSP (National Institute of Public Health) with religious leaders of the town of Bunia around the MVE response (challenges, community buy-in and implemented public health actions).

Continuation of support to affected provinces under the leadership of the IM and members of SGI based in Bunia, Ituri province.

Field visit in the ZS of Mongbwalu under the lead of the DG of the INSP, accompanied by the COUSP Coordinator, IM as well as technical and financial partners (OCHA, PNUD, PAM, UNICEF, OMS).

Closure of the training of the first group of 23 head doctors of ZS on the zonal approach and ACs on community surveillance.

## 4.3 Laboratory

Ituri: 115 new samples collected and analysed (positivity 39,1%; n=45)

Nord-Kivu: 146 results remain pending due to a shortage of reagents.

Sud-Kivu: 6 samples received and analysed in the laboratory, all negative for MVE.

## 4.4 Infection Prevention and Control (PCI)

Ituri: Scorecard evaluation in 19 ESS of the ZSs of Bunia (1 ESS: 38,7%), Mongbwalu (2 ESS: 11% and 12%), Bambu (16 ESS: all <50,0%); start of the training of 50 healthcare providers (20 supervisors and 30 focal points) from 16 ESS of the ZS of Bunia on PCI; opening of 3 rings around confirmed cases in the ZSs of Bunia (households, ESS and other identified public places: 10/11 identified sites, decontaminated), Rwampara (households, ESS and church identified: 8/9 identified sites decontaminated) and Mongbwalu (12/17 households were decontaminated): briefing of 19 healthcare providers (CS Nyakasanza, CS Bunia Cité), on waste management, hand hygiene, bio-cleaning, 10 providers from CS Bora Uzima on donning and doffing PPE and 5 other providers from the AS (health area) Ndibakudu (PS Arche de Noé and la Grâce de Dieu) on general notions of MVE; briefing of 9 surface technicians (TS) on MVE and PCI standard precautions.

Nord-Kivu: 2/4 ESS decontaminated around 2 confirmed cases in Katwa; 3 households identified and planned for decontamination in Katwa; 7/8 ESS supported and 37 providers were briefed on PCI topics in these ESS.

Sud-Kivu: Decontamination of the intensive care unit of HGR (general referral hospital) KATANA and the cantonment site of Nyakadaka; scorecard evaluation of ESS Kalagane (40,0%) and CM Joponika (9,7%) followed by the development of improvement plans; briefing of 12 providers from HGR Katana on decontamination, donning and doffing PPE; evaluation of 5 hot spots and installation of handwashing facilities in the health zone of Mitimurhesa.

## 4.5 Holistic care

13 deaths recorded in CTE (Ebola treatment centre)/CT (transit centre)/CI (isolation centre)/ESS including 9 confirmed cases (1 at CME, 1 in Rwampara: a 9-week pregnant woman, 4 in Mongbwalu, 1 at Elikya and 1 in Bambu) and 4 suspected including 2 PPL (person released from treatment (discharged patient)) (1 at CME, 1 Bambu, 1 Nyankunde and 1 Elikya).

Five (5) children from the Saint-Nicolas orphanage, declared non-cases after 2 negative results at CTE CME.

3 newly cured at CTE CME of the ZS of Rwampara (Ituri province).

Thus, the cumulative total of cured individuals rises from 19 to 22, including 20 in Ituri province and 2 in Nord-Kivu (Goma and Katwa).

## 4.6 Continuity of services.

Following the evaluation of 5 ESS Mongbwalu, several challenges and/or gaps were identified.

Among the 5 evaluated ESS, 3 (CECCA-20, Mongbwalu and Abelkozo) do not have adequate infrastructure and 1 (CS rather) requires rehabilitation of the dispensary.

Finalisation of improvement plans for the 3 ESS (Komanda, Mambasa and Mongbwalu) previously evaluated.

## 4.7 CREC

Nord-Kivu: 13 251 people reached through MVE prevention awareness via door-to-door and mass activities; 7 589 households visited including 3 200 with two visits and practical demonstration (handwashing, temperature check, safe handling) with more than 30 356 people reached; 974 ReCos (community health worker) mobilised; 212 community actors briefed on CREC and SBC and infodemic management; 15 alerts reported (12 validated ≤ 48h, 3 undergoing verification) in addition to a rumour clarified with community feedback; 50 community radio stations broadcast three formats on prevention measures against MVE.

Sud-Kivu: Mass awareness-raising of 1 252 schoolchildren (637 boys and 615 girls) from the primary school KABUNGA in the health area Kavumu/ZS of Mitimurhesa on prevention measures and signs of Ebola virus disease; advocacy with 23 teachers and a headteacher to intensify awareness in the school environment; briefing of 14 youth U-reporters volunteers on CREC interventions around cases in the health area Kahungu/ZS of Mitimurhesa affected by MVE; 10 radio channels broadcast prevention messages against MVE; 640 community leaders and community relays committed to supporting public health actions in the health zone of Mitimurhesa.

Ituri: Organisation of a community dialogue by the DG of the INSP with religious leaders of the town of Bunia; 177 people reached including 80 (40 community actors from the ZS of Bunia and 49 ReCos from the ZS of Rwampara) during the briefing on MVE preventive measures and community-based surveillance and 97 religious leaders (47 women included) during a training on MVE preventive measures in religious settings; 2 advocacy sessions organised with 20 people in the ZSs of Bunia (10 people: market leaders of BIGO, Yambi Yaya, Nyakasanza) and Nizi (10 people: The head of the IDP site at LOPA) respectively around their involvement in MVE prevention activities in public places and their buy-in to the response (contact tracing included); 5 mass awareness sessions organised, 385 people reached (187 M and 161 W) in 7 ZS with topics on MVE preventive measures, the importance of EDS, reporting of community alerts, etc.

Support to other pillars: Surveillance: Contact listing (As Mongbwalu/ ZS Mongbwalu); investigation and pre-listing of contacts (AS Mudzimaria/ ZS Bunia,).

PCI: To prepare buy-in for EDS (ZS of Bunia and Rwampara, Result: EDS performed) and for decontaminations (performed).

Community feedback: (i) A voice message accompanied by a photo and messages of a doctor who died (confirmed Ebola case) yesterday at CME, which went viral, is creating countless negative comments on the quality and reliability of MVE care centres; (ii) several identified truck drivers belonging to a tribe often refuse handwashing at the TCHAY control point and spread messages denying the disease.

Recommendations were formulated for adequate and targeted responses.

## 4.8 Logistics and Security

Supply of inputs to 31 ESS/ZS and medicines (critical items) to 5 ZS.

135 motorcycles ensure mobility of field teams across different ZSs and pillars.

34 vehicles (2 functional ambulances.) ensure mobility of coordination, of field teams in the different ZSs.

## 4.9. Security

The security situation in the town of Bunia (health zones of Bunia and Rwampara) is relatively calm.

However, the presence of armed groups in the territories of Djugu, Irumu and Mambasa continues to limit humanitarian access in several affected or at-risk health zones.

## 4.10. PSEA (Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse)

Start of awareness activities by the PSEA pillar in the town of Goma in Nord-Kivu.

Briefing in Bunia of MCZs and ACs of 23/36 Health Zones of DPS Ituri on protection from sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment and signing of the declaration of commitment.

Briefing of 84 PAM staff and security officers (27 women and 57 men) in the ZS of Bunia, 20 participants (5 women and 15 men), 95 healthcare providers (51 women and 44 men) from the ZS Karisimbi in Goma.

Briefing of ACoDD (the Afnet team) and PoE experts, a total of 13 participants (2 women, 11 men).

In Miti-Murhesa in the ZS of Katana 208 participants were sensitised on PEAHS.

PSEA awareness-raising at EP Kabuga, more than 1000 pupils sensitised (Sud-Kivu).

# 5. MAIN CHALLENGES


| No. | Challenges | Impact | Required action |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Reluctance regarding post-mortem samples (swabs) | Delayed confirmation; underestimation of cases | Intensive community engagement; involvement of religious leaders |
| 2 | Insufficient capacity in standard-compliant CTEs despite the opening of Rwampara | Potential saturation of existing CTEs | Accelerated construction of planned CTEs |
| 3 | Weakness of contact tracing (overall rate 56,3%, target 95%) | Interruption of transmission chains compromised | Training, deployment and motivation of community relays |
| 4 | Lack of supply of Generic Essential Medicines (MEG) in targeted HGRs | Weakening of holistic care | Advocacy for MEG provision |
| 5 | Insufficiency of PCI materials (PPE, DLM, chlorine) in Nord-Kivu | Nosocomial risk | Urgent supply |
| 6 | Low reporting of alerts in the 3 provinces | Delayed case detection | Strengthening of community surveillance |
| 7 | Insufficiency of financial resources for all pillars | Slowdown of operations | Resource mobilisation (gap of 21,5 million USD) |
